visuals.heading: Key Ideas at a Glance

items.text: Most students and even most working engineers hear about one CS career: software developer.
That ordering is not useful for a decision.

blocks.heading: Ordered By Growth

items.text: Most "career options in CS" lists are ordered by how impressive the job title sounds, or by which one the writer heard about first.

The tracks below are ordered by a different question: which ones have real, current headroom to scale toward significantly higher income or seniority, versus which ones are structurally capped or already getting more crowded at the door.
Building, deploying, and maintaining the models and pipelines behind AI features, not just training something in a notebook, but getting it into production, monitoring it, and keeping it useful.

blocks.sourceSectionTitle: The 9 real computer science career tracks, ordered by growth, not prestige

blocks.heading: Every Track Above Except One Is Bound

items.text: Building your own SaaS product, or running a development and consulting practice, is different.
This track scales for three concrete reasons, not because "entrepreneurship sounds exciting."

blocks.sourceSectionTitle: The one CS track where your income is not capped by hours

blocks.heading: Competition Never Really Ends

items.text: Most career advice treats "getting in" as the hard part and everything after as smooth sailing.
For three tracks on this map, that is simply false.
Stage one: Getting a profile strong enough to be noticed at all, a top engineering college via JEE, or a serious competitive-programming or olympiad-level record.

blocks.sourceSectionTitle: Where the competition never really ends

blocks.heading: Questions Before You Commit to One Track

items.text: The four questions reduces the cost of a confident-but-wrong first guess.
Can you handle the daily reality of this track, heads-down building versus infra firefighting versus stakeholder meetings versus long research cycles.
Do not choose a track whose actual daily work you already know you would hate.

blocks.heading: CS Degree for Each of These Tracks
blocks.sourceSectionTitle: Do you need a CS degree for each of these tracks?

rows: A recognised engineering degree is a hard requirement here, GATE and most PSU exams are built on top of it. There is no self-taught substitute for this door.

A strong CS or math-heavy degree is heavily preferred and, for quant specifically, brand of college matters a great deal. Self-taught practitioners do get hired, but usually need a stronger portfolio or competition record than a degree-holder needs.
Effectively required, a PhD is the credential the track is built around.
A degree helps with the first filter at large companies, but shipped work, certifications, and a clear project history can substitute for a weaker-brand degree more than in the tracks above.
Your own SaaS or consulting practice
The most degree-agnostic track here. Clients and users care about the product and the delivery, not your transcript.

blocks.heading: Do a CS Degree

items.text: Do a CS degree, learn to code, become a software developer.
If you're good at coding, software development is automatically your best option.
AI/ML, cybersecurity, and product are "extra" specialisations you pick up later, if at all.
Government and research careers barely get mentioned next to private-sector coding jobs.

blocks.sourceSectionTitle: Why "computer science career options" is a bigger map than most people are shown

blocks.heading: Boilerplate Code: CRUD Endpoints, Config Scaffolding, Basic

items.text: Simple bug fixes and pattern-based refactors spread across a codebase.
First-pass manual QA and repetitive support-ticket triage.
"I can write working code" as a standalone differentiator on a resume.

blocks.sourceSectionTitle: What AI is already automating in CS work, and where it multiplies you

blocks.heading: IT Job and Want a Stronger Track

items.text: Turn ticket handling, support work, or QA into a visible artifact: an automation script, a dashboard, a documented fix with a before-and-after.
Pick one of the nine tracks to specialise in, instead of collecting five trending skills at once with none of them deep enough to show.
If your target is a name-brand product company, remember the two-stage reality above: clearing that interview loop is real progress, and the senior/staff bar afterward is a separate, later climb.
Use your service-company exposure honestly, delivery discipline, production reality, and client handling are real assets, even if the current role feels invisible on paper.
